thread.title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Cut Amid Soft iPhone Sales | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Gets Price-Target Cut Amid Soft iPhone Sales | Investor's Business Daily
text:
A Wall Street analyst on Wednesday trimmed his price target on Apple stock amid reports that iPhone sales weakness has continued since the December quarter.
X D.A. Davidson analyst Tom Forte reiterated his buy rating on Apple ( AAPL ) but lowered his 12-to-18-month price target to 245 from 260.
Apple stock rose 0.4% to 153.92 on the stock market today . On Oct. 3, Apple stock hit a record high of 233.47.
Forte trimmed his iPhone sales estimates for 2019 after hearing comments from Apple suppliers that suggested iPhone sales softness has continued into the new year.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Declining iPhone Sales Ahead "We are lowering our estimates for all four calendar quarters in 2019 on the expectation that iPhone sales weakness from the December 2018 period will persist in calendar 2019," Forte said in a report. "Our new estimates reflect year-over-year unit sales declines of 8.5%, 6.9%, 4.8%, and 2.0% for the March through December 2019 quarters, respectively. We project average selling prices to decline by 3.0%, 3.0%, 3.0% and 0.5%, over the same timeframe."
Apple will report fiscal first-quarter results after the market close on Tuesday. On Jan. 2 , Apple pre-announced weaker-than-expected sales for the quarter ended Dec. 29. It blamed the revenue shortfall on disappointing iPhone sales, mostly in China.
Apple's December-quarter report will be the first one where it won't give hardware unit sales figures. The Cupertino, Calif.-based company wants to shift attention to growing sales of services and accessories.
